contract: Convert a one-minute-plus-seconds lap to seconds, then subtract a faster-runner difference crossing the minute boundary. Keep calendar/elapsed-time interpretation, not a speed model.
Recover purchase cost from amount paid and change, then divide by weight to obtain price per pound. Two contextual operations precede the unit rate.
Find cents per ounce for A, add B's unit-price premium, scale to the requested ounces and convert cents to dollars. Preserve the full operation chain.
Divide total lodging cost by a positive whole number of nights; the generated nightly rate is integral.
Convert large whole-number yards to feet with factor 3. Number-size practice, not a distinct dimension or a course-based rank.
Scale a seed price proportionally and round only the final money amount to cents, halfway upward; do not round the intermediate unit rate.
Divide total earnings from two different hour/rate groups by total hours. Unequal weights prohibit taking the simple mean of the two rates.
Scale a grape price proportionally and round only the final cost to cents, halfway upward. Preserve exact intermediate ratios.
Cube an integer side-length ratio from 2 through 5 to obtain the ratio of cube volumes. No area ratio or inverse-root branch occurs here.
Convert feet to yards by division by 3; the generated whole-number amount is a multiple of 30.
Convert a whole-number multiple of 12 inches to an integral number of feet.
Convert whole-number feet to inches by multiplying by 12.
Convert multiples of 528 feet to tenths of a mile using 5280 feet per mile; the output need not be integral.
Convert 101 through 990 centimeters to meters, retaining hundredths where needed.
Convert grams to kilograms; generated amounts give exact whole kilograms.
Calculate two distance/time rates in the same units and subtract their exact rational values. There is no hours-to-minutes conversion.
Convert multiples of 100 milliliters to liters, retaining a tenths-place result.
Interpret bushels per acre as total yield divided by acreage. This is a unit rate, not an unweighted mean of field yields.
Average four money bills; generated cent totals are divisible by four. Preserve decimal money notation.
Use the supplied hits/at-bats formula and round the final batting average to the nearest thousandth. This is a contextual rate, not a list mean.
Combine two groups using their unequal counts and means, then round the final result to hundredths.
Recover the total required for an overall target mean, subtract the existing total, and divide by five future quizzes. Existing group size varies from three to seven.
Count fair-die outcomes for equality, less-than, greater-than or different-from events. Strict bounds and the different-from values above six allow certain or impossible events.
Find the probability of a specified run of two through five identical fair-coin faces; independence gives one divided by two to the run length.

Two-card sampling without replacement includes same-suit, neither-face, both-face, same-color and face-plus-specified-rank in either order. Only the last branch adds the reverse order; no uniform rank against ordered cards is claimed.
Find the rain complement by subtracting a stated percentage from 100 percent.
Convert favorable-to-unfavorable odds a:b to a/(a+b) for the same named event, which may itself be not-winning. Do not automatically complement the named event.
Given winning odds, answer either winning or not-winning according to the branch. The complement branch is optional, so do not assert a uniform extra-step difficulty over same-event odds.
Average four whole numbers of varying digit lengths by sum divided by four.
Recover an unknown shop price from the stated mean and five through seven shops; subtract all known prices from the target total.
Average three masses with three decimal places; the generated sum is divisible by three in thousandths.
Average two lengths with three decimal places; retain an exact decimal mean.
For one marble draw, add the counts of two distinct colors; the events are disjoint, so there is no intersection correction.
Previous independent die results are irrelevant to the next less-than or greater-than event. Count strict bounds, including impossible/certain cases.
For two same-color draws with replacement, multiply k/n by k/n. Both numerator and denominator reset.

Two-card sampling without replacement includes five event branches, with face-then-specified-rank ordered in the last branch. Other branches overlap the either-order recipe; retain related-only ordering between these two mixed recipes.
Find range, mean, median and mode of eight through eleven values. The unique mode occurs three times; even/odd counts change the median operation.
Find range, mean, median and mode of weight data with eight through eleven values, a unique triple mode, and both even/odd median branches.
Find range, mean, median and mode of score data with eight through eleven values, a unique triple mode, and both even/odd median branches.
Recover the mean of four values from their supplied total; two supplied individual values are irrelevant.
Combine two groups from their counts and means; compute the exact weighted total divided by combined count.
Combine three groups from their counts and means; retain all three weights and the exact combined mean.
Compute a weighted score from two given percentage weights totaling 100; do not substitute group counts or assume equal weights.
Count the ordered two-dice outcomes with a specified sum from one through twelve. Sum one is impossible; the sample space has 36 outcomes.
Ignore earlier repetitions and give the probability of a specified face on the next fair-die roll.
Earlier marbles were replaced; ignore those results when calculating the probability of the next specified color.
Calculate the probability of one exact ordered three- or four-toss coin sequence. All-heads is a possible branch; no permutation factor is needed.
For different colors without replacement, retain the second color count but reduce the total by one.
Calculate both with-replacement and without-replacement probabilities for two different colors, preserving the requested answer order.
Calculate both without-replacement and with-replacement probabilities for the same color. Without replacement decreases both its numerator and the total.
From labeled whole-number rectangle sides, calculate both perimeter and area; distinguish linear and square units.
Find right-triangle area from the two perpendicular legs. The labeled hypotenuse is a distractor, not an altitude requirement.
Combine a square and right triangle; infer the triangular base as total length minus square side, then sum component areas.
Find parallelogram area from base and perpendicular height; the slanted side is irrelevant.
Find circumference from radius using pi=22/7; radii are multiples of seven, so the result is exact.
Find rectangular prism volume from three labeled perpendicular dimensions.
Find a right-trapezoid area from two parallel bases and its perpendicular height; use half the base sum times height.
A convex n-gon triangulates from one vertex into n-2 triangles; n ranges from five through ten.
Calculate a convex polygon's interior-angle sum as (n-2) times 180 degrees.
Calculate a regular polygon's exterior angle as 360/n; the side count divides 360 exactly.
Find cylinder volume for radius two through five and height seven through thirteen, using pi=3.14 exactly and perpendicular height.
From a right triangle with Pythagorean-triple legs, find both its area and missing hypotenuse. This adds a second geometric construct to area calculation.
Calculate rectangular prism surface area by summing three pairs of equal rectangular faces.
Complete an axis-aligned rectangle from three consecutive signed-coordinate vertices, across four vertex-order variants, and calculate its area from coordinate differences.
Find oblique-triangle area from a supplied external perpendicular altitude and base; do not use a slanted side.
From radius, find both circumference and area with pi=3.14 exactly.
From diameter, first recover radius, then give radius, circumference and area with pi=3.14 exactly; half-integer radii can occur.
Select the graph matching y=mx+b among four sign variations; slope is nonzero rational and intercept is nonzero signed. Selection does not require authoring a graph.
Select the bar graph matching all six table frequencies assigned to grades; comparing one bar alone is insufficient.
Find cylinder volume for radius two through eight and height three through fifteen, using pi=3.14 exactly. Same formula, broader bounded arithmetic than the other cylinder recipe.
Find rectangular prism surface area from three positive integer dimensions. Sum all six faces, not volume or lateral area alone.
Average three scores, each a multiple of five.
Sort five values and report the middle value; duplicates are permitted.
Find sphere volume for radius two through fifteen with pi=3.14; round only the final result to hundredths, halfway upward.
Scale circle circumference by a central-angle fraction for radius three through nine and angles 6,12,18,24,30 or 60 degrees; final hundredths rounding is required and no diagram is supplied.
Recognize segment, ray, line, angle, parallel lines or intersecting lines from endpoint/arrow conventions in a supplied drawing.
Read one histogram-bin frequency from five intervals with frequencies two through ten; do not interpret a bar as one raw observation.
Convert a labeled circle-graph percentage into a voter count; the voter total is a multiple of 100.
Recover an off-axis point reflected across the y-axis while an on-axis point stays fixed; output the missing coordinate pair.
Classify a labeled triangle by the most specific side category: equilateral, exactly-two-equal isosceles, or scalene.
Select the image of a rectangle after 90-degree counterclockwise, 180-degree, or 90-degree clockwise rotation about the origin; no drawing is requested.
Reflect all three triangle vertices across the x-axis and supply six coordinate values.
Translate four rectangle vertices by a signed vector and supply eight coordinate values.
Calculate one interior angle of a regular polygon as 180-360/n.
Calculate one exterior angle of a regular polygon as 360/n.
Count diagonals from one vertex as n-3, not all n(n-3)/2 polygon diagonals.
Classify a displayed angle from 30 through 180 degrees as acute, right, obtuse or straight.
Recognize the right angle among four supplied diagrams; this is a single-class selection task.
Select the histogram matching all five interval frequencies in a table, rather than reading one frequency.
Classify the smaller clock-hand angle at a whole hour from one through eleven; use 30-degree steps and the smaller angle.
Identify the segment passing through the circle center with both endpoints on the circumference; rotation of the drawing does not change diameter.

Evaluate six similarity statements, including squares versus arbitrary rectangles, corresponding angles, possible unequal size and non-required equal area or side lengths. True/false recognition is not justification.
Select the missing information needed to recover Lee's April hours from the given comparison; do not invent a quantity.
Organize fifteen two-digit values into the supplied stems two through five with sorted leaves and duplicates; the stems and key are already provided.
Read and sort all fifteen observations from a stem-and-leaf display, retaining duplicate leaves and the supplied key.
From a stem-and-leaf display of nine values with one triple mode, calculate median, mode and range.
Select the correct box plot for nine strictly increasing observations; exclude the overall median when finding quartiles.
Read range and interquartile range from a supplied box plot by two differences.
Read minimum, maximum, first quartile, third quartile and median from a box plot in the explicitly requested order.
Name the month between two stated months in the same year; this recipe never crosses December.
Judge whether one of five conditions establishes a parallelogram. Both opposite pairs equal or diagonals bisecting are sufficient; a kite condition or one equal opposite pair is not.
Identify SAS then CPCTC for the supplied split-triangle diagram with equal halves and a common perpendicular side. Abbreviations alone are requested, not a complete proof.
Read the mean at the center and the standard deviation from label spacing on a normal curve; mean 63-69 and standard deviation 3 or 4.
Select the compass chord-transfer step for copying an angle after equal-radius arcs are already given; do not equate this with constructing the whole copy.
Select the final straightedge step for an angle bisector after equal-radius intersecting arcs are supplied.

The generator alternates pyramid, cone and sphere volume; sphere has no perpendicular-height input and cone/sphere require final hundredths rounding. Keep these mixed demands related rather than imposing one uniform rank.
Calculate sphere surface area as four pi r squared with pi=3.14 exactly.
Read AB and nonzero-start BC on an eighth-inch ruler and subtract their lengths. Preserve the distinction between a tick coordinate and a segment length.
Find square-pyramid volume from square side and perpendicular height, divided by three. Slant height is not given or needed.
Find cone volume from radius and perpendicular height in millimeters, pi=3.14, rounded only at the end to hundredths.
Find square-pyramid surface area from square base side and supplied slant height; sum base plus four triangular faces.
Find cone total surface area including the base from radius and supplied slant height, using pi=3.14 exactly.
Read a zero-origin inch ruler at sixteenth-inch ticks from 2 through 61 and give the reduced fractional length; no physical drawing is required.
Read a metric ruler at tenths of a centimeter from 1.5 through 4.7 centimeters; no physical drawing is required.
Find distance between distinct signed-coordinate points from -8 through 8, reporting an exact simplified radical or integer when the radicand is a square.
Read a protractor with baseline zero or 180 degrees; choose the scale aligned with the baseline and give the smaller angle.
Report the dimension count of a point, line, rectangle or rectangular prism, including zero dimensions for a point.
Classify supplied lines as parallel, perpendicular or oblique; the oblique branch intersects but not at right angles.
Classify angles with numerical degree labels among acute/right/obtuse/straight, including 90 and 180 degrees.
For an inch divided into 2,4,8 or 16 intervals, state the smallest graduation 1/n inch. Graduation is not an accuracy or error-bound claim.
Choose a plausible everyday length, capacity, mass or temperature estimate from three alternatives. These different attributes do not support one uniform numerical difficulty rank.
Using one of seven US unit equivalences, express one smaller unit as a percentage of a larger unit, including fractional percentages.
Classify a numerically labeled angle, including acute/right/obtuse/straight boundary values. Same executable body as lesson 7.4, original identity retained.
Convert a proper fraction of a circle into both numerical percent and central-angle degrees; denominators vary from 2 to 12 among specified choices.
Name a three-, four-, five-, six-, eight- or ten-sided polygon from its diagram and side count.
Name all vertices of a polygon consecutively, permitting cyclic shifts and reversal but not diagonal jumps; teacher-reviewed response.
Distinguish regular and irregular three-, five- or six-sided polygons from a to-scale drawing; regularity needs equal sides and angles.

Compare rectangles or triangles for similarity in the phase-2 override, including a deliberately altered corresponding side. Justify corresponding ratios and angles; a yes/no response alone is insufficient.
Compare rectangles or triangles for congruence in the phase-2 override, including equal and scaled cases. Justify equal corresponding parts, not just shape.
Evaluate six phase-2 statements distinguishing similarity and congruence; true/false recognition does not constitute a proof.
Divide a regular polygon's perimeter by its three, four, five, six or eight equal sides to recover one side length.
Distinguish linear centimeters from square centimeters as length versus area units. This is dimensional vocabulary, not formula calculation.
Recover a square side from a supplied perfect-square area; take the positive root.
Recover a square side from its perimeter, then square it to find area. This combines two measure formulas.
Explain why metric relationships use powers of ten and supply a correct factor-10,100 or1000 example with units; teacher-reviewed explanation.
Compare Celsius and Fahrenheit temperatures using the supplied affine conversion, including equal cases and negative Celsius values. The comparison, not just substitution, is required.
Physically draw/cut a triangle's corners and arrange them on a straight line to demonstrate the 180-degree sum; measurement demonstration is not a formal general proof.
Name complementary, supplementary, adjacent or vertical angles from definitions; adjacency alone does not specify a numerical sum.
Find an unknown numerical complementary, supplementary or vertical angle in the phase-2 branches. The vertical branch copies the value rather than subtracting.
Write both reciprocal unit multipliers for a stated equivalence and explain why each is one. No numerical conversion result is requested.
Express a constant travel rate in both distance/time and reciprocal time/distance with correct units; teacher review checks the reciprocal interpretation.
Draw every and only symmetry line of an equilateral/scalene triangle or square/nonsquare rectangle in the phase-2 override; zero, two, three and four lines can occur.
Find the other three angles of a parallelogram using equal opposite and supplementary adjacent angles.
Measure three real circular objects, tabulate circumference/diameter ratios and discuss measurement error when estimating pi. No fabricated observations; distinct experimental demand stays unranked.
Give decimal and fractional approximations to pi and explain neither is exactly pi. This is conceptual explanation, not a calculation hierarchy.
Name six solid diagrams in the phase-2 override: rectangular prism, cylinder, sphere, cone, square pyramid and triangular prism.
Count faces, edges and vertices of either an n-gonal prism or pyramid for n=3,4,5,6 in the phase-2 override; formulas differ by solid type.
Draw an n-gonal prism in perspective for n=3,4,5; label its two congruent parallel bases and show hidden edges with dashed lines.
Draw every diagonal of a convex four-, five-, six- or eight-sided polygon and report n(n-3)/2. Count each nonadjacent vertex pair once.
Estimate a displayed angle within ten degrees without a protractor and justify familiar benchmarks; do not treat an exact measurement answer as meeting this method.
Identify corresponding, alternate-interior, same-side-interior or vertical angle pairs by their positions on a transversal diagram.
Calculate both curved semicircle arc length, excluding diameter, and semicircle area with pi=3.14. The two-output demand differs from arc-only tasks.
Find sphere surface area from a labeled radius with pi=3.14 exactly.
Physically construct two concentric circles with different given radii, keep a fixed compass center and label that center.
Inscribe a regular hexagon by stepping a compass radius, then join alternate vertices for an equilateral triangle; retain construction arcs.
Construct four, six or eight equal circle sectors in the phase-2 override using compass and straightedge, retain arcs and explain equal angles.
Measure a central and corresponding inscribed angle on a supplied drawing within three degrees and compare the 2:1 relationship; measurement is not a general theorem proof.
Name radius, diameter, chord or arc from a verbal definition; a diameter is a special chord, not any center-to-circle segment.
Identify all four quadrants, the axes or the origin from signed coordinate pairs in seven phase-2 branches.
Draw a double-line graph for four days of scores for each of two teams; shared uniform axes, ordered segments and a distinguishing key are required.
Construct a circle graph from counts using a protractor in the phase-2 override, with totals eight or twelve, complete labels and angle tolerance three degrees.
Draw all symmetry lines of a square, nonsquare rectangle or nonsquare rhombus, including the no-diagonal symmetry of a nonsquare rectangle.
Locate the fixed parallelogram's diagonal midpoint and justify point symmetry by a 180-degree rotation; no variable family of centers is generated.
Write formulas for rectangle perimeter and area, evaluate both, and distinguish linear from square units; teacher-reviewed formula production adds to numerical calculation.
Check whether three lengths form a right triangle by comparing squares; branches are scaled 3-4-5 triples or a longest side increased by one.
Calculate sphere volume with pi=3.14 for radii that are multiples of three, yielding an exact finite decimal rather than requiring final rounding.
Convert cubic centimeters to both milliliters and liters using the stated capacity equivalences; dimensional interpretation is part of the context.
Use the explicitly assumed water density exactly 1 g/cm3 to convert milliliters to both grams and kilograms. Do not generalize this density to all substances or conditions.
Distinguish zero divided by a nonzero number from division by zero, including 0/0 being undefined due to no unique quotient.
Find the excluded x for 5/(x-a) from a signed integer shift; the denominator must not be zero.
From favorable odds a:b, give both the event and complement probabilities in that order.
Name the preceding or following month, including December/January wraparound; preserve both index branches.
Read a Celsius thermometer from zero through forty in five-degree graduations.
Name triangle, rectangle, square or circle using the most specific name; the nonsquare rectangle has unequal adjacent lengths.
From twelve raw observations, tally three explicit interval categories then draw separated bars with labeled axes and a uniform scale.

Calculate a date after a stated number of days; branches include within-month arithmetic and crossing a month/year boundary, with leap-year February. Do not rank this entire mixed recipe as always harder than same-month tasks.
Design a neutral preference survey, choose respondents, prepare a tally table and state a generalization limit; collect no invented results. No numerical mean or graph ranking is implied.
Determine whether price and count suffice for total cost; explain the missing count or calculate when present. Both sufficient/insufficient branches matter.
Convert one through four quarter-turns into clockwise degrees, including a full revolution.
Draw at least six congruent square or equilateral-triangle tiles and explain a 360-degree vertex sum with no gaps/overlaps; distinct construction/reasoning demand.

Estimate rectangle perimeter, rectangle area or rectangular prism volume after rounding each dimension to tens. The mixed-dimensional branches stay related, not uniformly ranked against an exact formula task.
Infer a uniform scale step of 2,5,10 or20 and calculate the value at a stated interval from zero; this is scale reading without a supplied diagram.
Draw a given angle using a protractor, then bisect it with compass and straightedge, retain arcs and state each half-angle. The full construction is teacher-reviewed.
Choose the closest benchmark 0,1/2 or1 for one of five twentieths values, including 21/20; compare distances without rounding to an unrestricted half-integer.
Convert whole cubic feet to cubic inches by cubing 12, not multiplying by 12 once.

Show three or six unit multipliers for cubic feet/yards/miles to cubic inches or the reverse. Accept exact products/fractions and reverse every factor; mixed lengths of chain preclude a uniform one-step-versus-six-step rank.
Convert a multiple of 1000 cm3 to both m3 and liters, distinguishing the cubed length factor from the capacity factor.
Name compass and unmarked straightedge as the permitted tools for classical construction; naming tools alone does not demonstrate their use.
Read two adjacent histogram frequencies from a four-bin display and add them, including possible zero counts.
Plot P(x,y), Q(y,x), R(0,x), identify quadrants/axis and explain swapped pairs coincide exactly when x=y. Retain signed nonzero x,y and the required explanation.

Alternate real-domain tasks: a principal square root needs a nonnegative radicand; a rational expression retains all original exclusions even after cancellation. Keep mixed branch demands related, not uniformly above one denominator exclusion.
Model simultaneous opposite-direction travel by adding both distances, write the equation and solve the common elapsed time; there is no delayed departure in this sum recipe.
Give parallel, intersecting and skew prism-edge examples and the intersection of two planes, explaining noncoplanarity for skew lines. Spatial reasoning is not ordered by course title.
Compute population standard deviation of five signed values using denominator N=5, not N-1, including constant data with zero deviation; round only final sigma to hundredths.
From a given normal mean and standard deviation, find endpoints within one,two or three standard deviations and the corresponding approximate 68/95/99.7 percentage.
Draw and label line, ray and segment with correct arrows, endpoint counts and finite/infinite length descriptions. This is production, not visual recognition.
Draw a rectangle with an interior circular hole and calculate remaining area using pi=3.14; subtract the hole exactly once.

Given base area and perpendicular height, find cone or cylinder volume, with the one-third factor only for the cone. Mixed solid types are related to dimensional-formula tasks, not universally easier.
For two intersecting lines, find the other three angles in cyclic order using both supplementary and vertical relationships.
Alternate inverse-solid tasks: recover sphere diameter from symbolic-pi surface area, or cylinder height from symbolic-pi volume. Different inverse operations prevent one uniform difficulty stage.
Find total surface area of a right triangular prism with a scaled 3-4-5 base: two triangles plus three rectangles.
Draw and label a circle's radius, diameter, non-diameter chord, minor/major arc and central/inscribed angles; preserve point and arc distinctions.
Compose two stated implications about rectangles and parallelograms, and provide a counterexample to the converse. Deduction/converse reasoning is distinct from numerical geometry.
State the Euclidean parallel postulate in point-off-line form and apply its uniqueness to rule out two distinct parallels; conceptual justification, not a construction.
Find a triangle exterior angle by adding its two remote interior angles; do not apply a regular-polygon 360/n formula.
Find two missing cyclic-quadrilateral angles using supplementary opposite angles, not the parallelogram equal-opposite rule.
Find an adjacent rhombus angle, a bisected vertex angle and a diagonal intersection angle; three properties are required.
Convert miles/hour to feet/second with two oppositely oriented unit factors and round the final result to hundredths.
Convert yards to meters with three exact length factors, preserving unit cancellation.
Convert square yards to square meters with four explicit factors using the derived exact feet-to-meters factor; square the complete length conversion.
At fixed gas temperature, compute pressure from P1 V1/V2 and report two significant figures in scientific notation, retaining trailing zeros and rounding only at the end.
At fixed gas temperature, compute volume from P1 V1/P2 and report three significant figures in scientific notation, retaining trailing zeros and rounding only at the end.
Model two unequal travel distances with a speed multiple and two-hour time difference; find both speeds and times, preserving which trip takes longer.
Model an equal-distance out-and-back trip with a return-speed multiple and total time; find both speeds rather than assuming average speed is the arithmetic mean.
Rearrange PV=nRT for moles with the supplied gas constant and compatible units; final three-decimal rounding only.
Rearrange PV=nRT for volume with the supplied gas constant and compatible units; final three-decimal rounding only.
Find perpendicular distance from a signed-coordinate point to a horizontal line; it is the absolute vertical-coordinate difference, not a general oblique-line distance formula.
